summary:
Topic: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an educational project that explores the machines and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and other parts of space. These machines were sent into space to explore, collect information, and help scientists understand other worlds. Even after their missions ended, they remained important parts of space exploration history. Our project brings their stories back to life by explaining what they were, why they were sent, what they discovered, and how they helped us learn about space. It reminds us that every machine has a story, and every discovery has a history.
details: ### Complete PPT Content – 7 Slides Abandoned But Not Forgotten | NASA Space Apps Challenge Below is the actual slide-wise content you can copy into your PPT. I've kept it professional, informative and suitable for explaining your project to NASA judges. ### Slide 1 – Project Introduction ![Blog](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/3axFIBPLsuuXSt11PTfUSSESz7y8h9KooGkHIjHKlYeaa1cZlL5iAPkKjGdSSbmDlNLO_RY6bw7RRng5f9_wPJg8VtGZzmH3LGmSXPl7WQtIfTMxS8fLVCaS4uA0FBEZo_hOB4u6SNSeM0CHXeVuDKkHHmPhIW4gcJQeA_IzCwyWf12JWn7kOBL7AIk60yMG?purpose=fullsize) ABANDONED BUT NOT FORGOTTEN Every Machine Has a Story. Every Mission Leaves a Legacy. Project Overview Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive digital space museum that explores human-made objects left behind during space exploration. Our platform brings together the history of lunar and Martian missions, including landers, rovers, scientific instruments and mission hardware. Our Mission: * Preserve the stories of past space missions. * Make abandoned space hardware discoverable. * Present scientific discoveries through interactive exploration. * Create awareness about humanity's legacy beyond Earth. ### Slide 2 – Understanding the Problem ![New Group Works to Preserve Apollo Lunar Landing Sites | Scientific American](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/2HTm7SqD8D1wDsRabF6RXMlga8NjMXmKmj9F3CEyZ816dxOyemhBY3hy9wpTU4BfpRDWF9PFUL-oogkQrKN22SBUUFaOh2A3ZwvugDucemHtsDTHnDUU9XZMmNit8weHfGaaYOi-aQGYjeG5cjo56Jq2koh_EiQThiVgFPBe18Lco0F3vzLi5b04yynobYRt?purpose=fullsize) What Happens When a Space Mission Ends? Space missions often leave behind equipment, landers, rovers and scientific instruments on planetary surfaces. However, their stories and scientific contributions are not always easy for students and the public to explore in one place. Key Challenges * Scattered Information: Mission records and historical information are available across different sources. * Lack of Visualization: Traditional archives do not always provide an immersive way to explore abandoned hardware. * Forgotten Mission Legacy: People often remember successful missions but overlook the equipment and experiments left behind. * Limited Accessibility: Understanding the history of space exploration can require navigating complex technical documents. Our Core Question: Can we transform abandoned space hardware into an interactive learning experience? ### Slide 3 – Our Solution: A Digital Space Museum ![3D Solar system simulator | MicroEval | Artificial Analysis](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/xbnvrRdRsE4JDaermpvFNI2FWKXPfiofBxVeUbiI6avyw7E0iEY_T6mcceJBMynA6UkjKBc9Q8tSRnLJqNd4qjlbsZsLiHaNx1WlrMCY4VbnkoPUZD0mQSxHcJ5kKMBPRf_VJ0uJn0Vj6wGvRUhmvUVTI5aCyDgbxSrUsCv_M0oeISwk9nk7MLkC7GdudqRA?purpose=fullsize) One Platform. Multiple Worlds. Countless Stories. We developed an interactive website that presents abandoned space mission hardware through an immersive digital museum. Our Solution Includes: * Solar System Exploration: Explore planets through an animated solar system. * Moon Archive: Discover lunar landers, Apollo hardware and scientific experiments. * Mars Archive: Explore retired Martian landers and rovers. * Mission Timeline: Understand the chronological development of space exploration. * Interactive Exhibits: Select individual objects to explore their history and scientific purpose. Our Approach: Instead of presenting information as ordinary text, we combine scientific knowledge, visual storytelling and interactive 3D environments. ### Slide 4 – Explore the Moon: Lunar Mission Legacy ![Argonne celebrates Apollo 11 anniversary and new moon rock study | Argonne National Laboratory](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ye8rBttFWqG4mp2wCWz4kNlVXzadxKb6QBCxW2LTluccAIIz0nlvTBlAFgXe4xnNopGMQk6RvzLNBx-B-_FVX0sURkWBx_dCGn95tXnq9YAywRnn_YUfBI2a0LMrEASOSfHcBQbLAslvIWbUTFdYXW6W3I257gEZsSBz-NJVACowkCihQMeysyzqvIpqF-Tx?purpose=fullsize) The Moon: A Historic Record of Human Exploration The Moon contains numerous human-made artifacts from robotic and crewed missions. Our website presents 22 lunar exhibits covering important objects from lunar exploration. Important Mission Examples | Mission / Hardware | Year | Scientific importance | | ------------------ | --------- | -------------------------------------------- | | Surveyor 3 | 1967 | Tested lunar soil and landing conditions | | Apollo 11 | 1969 | First crewed Moon landing | | Apollo 12 | 1969 | Visited Surveyor 3 and recovered parts | | ALSEP | 1969–1972 | Deployed long-term lunar science experiments | | Apollo 15 | 1971 | Used the Lunar Roving Vehicle | Important Scientific Facts * Surveyor 3 transmitted 6,326 television pictures. * Its soil experiments helped establish that the lunar surface could support an Apollo Lunar Module. * Apollo ALSEP experiment packages continued operating for up to eight years. * Apollo 12 astronauts recovered parts of Surveyor 3 for examination on Earth. Why It Matters: These artifacts help us understand lunar geology, engineering achievements and the history of space exploration. NASA Science +2 ### Slide 5 – Explore Mars: Robotic Mission Legacy ![Revisit NASA's Mars Pathfinder and Rover (360 View) | NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/x-HGM8Kvu-Qy-CWAwB3D47AWl8dJC0lWK8_SjMDkJAfaPFH91W-POkGQ94TUvwRfb-TLYdy86OuNTGZvAjnexO1789CnBADL1g9Jh3Pq04aNKJ7Ev9qfPa5XpPu82ql9erZL8oPJYZ53YmoTSjnJzutjq4r--_Hprt2QoohvX-Jan6DAEtWU4YRDWl3R3AHS?purpose=fullsize) Mars: Seven Historic Mission Exhibits Our Mars gallery showcases seven retired landers and rovers that contributed to our understanding of the Red Planet. Important NASA Missions | Mission | Year | Major contribution | | --------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | | Viking 1 | 1976 | First successful NASA landing on Mars | | Viking 2 | 1976 | Investigated Martian soil and atmosphere | | Mars Pathfinder | 1997 | Delivered the Sojourner rover | | Spirit | 2004 | Investigated Martian rocks and soil | | Opportunity | 2004 | Found geological evidence of past water | | Phoenix | 2008 | Investigated Martian soil and water ice | | InSight | 2018 | Studied the interior and seismic activity of Mars | Important Scientific Facts * Viking 1 landed on Mars on July 20, 1976. * Pathfinder deployed Sojourner, the first wheeled rover on Mars. * Spirit and Opportunity investigated evidence of ancient water activity. * Opportunity operated for almost 15 years. * InSight detected marsquakes and studied the planet's internal structure. Why It Matters: These missions helped scientists understand Mars' geological history, environment and potential habitability. NASA Science +3 ### Slide 6 – Interactive Technology & Website Features ![OnSight Tool Allows Scientists to Meet in 3D Mars Simulation – NASA Mars Exploration](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/_NKThMzV7wcjk_uMkMHDA99ZoyzQE8Xna055hlt41M_599PDEpcO5_P-bxwATLykirArApxcydPMuCfvoTYbwn6ByhsI-UkiGKlCkfQHYSjO339kwJRfGbXyOhSZo4fEsmKl1u0SGwuQB0ctX8ON1F0teZ7odJt9w-bMtOACpnwLtCIReoeSU1Tc6r8XFheE?purpose=fullsize) Experience Space Exploration, Not Just Read About It. Our website transforms historical mission information into an interactive digital experience. Key Features * Animated Solar System: Explore planets through an animated planetary visualization. * 3D Lunar Environment: Experience the Moon's surface and discover lunar mission exhibits. * 3D Martian Environment: Explore a Martian landscape containing historical landers and rovers. * Interactive Navigation: Drag to look around, scroll to zoom and use keyboard controls to navigate. * Exhibit Inspection: Click on mission objects to explore their information. * Mission Timeline: Discover missions according to their launch and exploration years. * Favorites & Replay: Save interesting exhibits and revisit the introductory experience. Technology & Design Approach Our platform combines: * 3D visualization and animation. * Interactive user interface. * Scientific and historical mission information. * Digital storytelling and educational exploration. The objective is to make space exploration more engaging, accessible and understandable. ### Slide 7 – Impact, Future Scope & Conclusion ![NASA sets its sights on creation of moon station - Earth.com](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/SpOoB9IErvf-DQKjDjkzYcRlUn6jx3oGaUd6-98ow2E08at3w7xgbJG-rpkj3ie7Bp1y32lVkBwWyON2yyhUrXFPYn2-c2M6De0rbn8xodzg3CtrNNpfDkuBcceQ9x8XP11RFPecPZQA9gaFulSKk6NiZRKY90csYYAeFQETg2pFkTvyVGbxHtyizV75GNg9?purpose=fullsize) Preserving the Past. Inspiring the Future. Our project creates an educational platform that connects historical space missions with future generations. Project Impact * Educational Impact: Helps students understand planetary exploration and space technology. * Scientific Awareness: Highlights the scientific contributions of retired space missions. * Historical Preservation: Creates a digital record of human-made artifacts beyond Earth. * Interactive Learning: Makes complex scientific information easier to understand. Future Scope * Expand the archive with more verified lunar and Martian artifacts. * Add accurate geographical coordinates for mission hardware. * Integrate official NASA mission datasets and images. * Include additional planetary missions and exploration destinations. * Develop more detailed 3D models and educational experiences. ### OUR VISION ### A Mission May End, But Its Legacy Lives Forever. Thank You · Questions & Discussion ### Important NASA references for your PPT Use these official sources in your final slide notes or reference section: * [NASA – Human Artifacts on the Moon](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/humanartifacts.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) * [NASA – Surveyor 3 Mission](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/surveyor-3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) * [NASA – Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/HamishALSEP.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com) * [NASA – Viking Project](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/viking/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) * [NASA – Mars Pathfinder](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-pathfinder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) * [NASA – Opportunity Rover](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mer-opportunity/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) ### My recommendation for your NASA judging presentation Keep your slides visually clean. Use the screenshots you shared as the main visuals, and don't put all the speaking information on the slides. The most important thing: Judges should understand three things: * What problem are you addressing? * What have you actually developed? * How does your platform make space exploration knowledge more accessible? Your strongest demonstration will be opening the animated Solar System, entering the Moon gallery, exploring a lunar exhibit, and then switching to the Mars surface. This shows the actual working experience rather than just describing an idea.
